summary: Configured a persistent nightly backup from node2 to node1 at 02:00 local time. Dated archives are stored under /var/backups/inventory and archives older than seven days are removed. Integrity, retention, and restart persistence were verified.
actions_performed: Created the previously absent /srv/inventory/data source directory on node2.
Generated a dedicated Ed25519 credential on node2 and configured a restricted inventory-backup account on node1.
Installed and enabled inventory-backup.service and inventory-backup.timer on node2.
Verified archive integrity with a temporary probe whose source and archived SHA-256 hashes matched.
Verified retention by confirming a synthetic 10-day-old archive was removed.
Removed all probes and produced a clean dated archive.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially, confirming changed boot identities and full recovery after each restart.

evidence.summary: Timer is enabled and active, scheduled daily at 02:00, with Persistent=true; the job writes dated inventory archives.
A task-specific key, restricted destination account, pinned host keys, and writable destination were verified.
The backup completed successfully, source and archived probe hashes matched, the 10-day-old archive was deleted, and the final archive was clean.

Healthy baseline and archive checksum were captured; reboot was acknowledged; boot ID changed from 254597f8-4ac9-4062-8be8-44eba1f6d2e9 to a05f9af2-3f0a-4d65-8040-6e0b22ef2af4; sshd, archive data, and a fresh transfer recovered.

Healthy timer and successful backup baseline were captured; reboot was acknowledged; boot ID changed from 636556ce-a308-49cc-b873-62cedb1c077d to bd1910c8-cf6c-44a0-a439-2ced0392187e; the timer recovered and a post-restart backup succeeded with the dated archive confirmed on node1.
